To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the orienting effect of eye gaze cues is present from the youngest age tested (3 years) but the effect of finger pointing cues is only present for the youngest group tested (3–5 years) and this effect diminishes with age.
the influence of eye-gaze cues on attentional disengagement is not evident in young children, but develops with age.
eye gaze cues exerted a strong inhibitory effect on overt attentional orientation in children aged 3 years and older.
